newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end higher on foreign-fund easing.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end higher on foreign-fund easing.

text.p: Taiwan share prices closed higher on Friday, helped by Wall Street's big surge but rising mainly on news that local regulators had raised the stock investment ceiling for individual foreign funds, brokers said.
The weighted index ended up 31.26 points or 0.46 percent at 6,890.66, off a high of 6,922.39.
Turnover was a relatively active T$44.2 billion.
The Securities and Exchange Commission on Thursday raised the foreign investment cap for individual funds to US$600 million from US$400 million.
"In a market that is entering consolidation, such news is a good indicator showing the government's position on the bullish side," said Amy Huang, an analyst at Nomura Securities.
Wall Street's overnight surge helped sentiment but was only secondary for Taiwan's local-minded investors, brokers said.

Financials rose most, up 1.04 percent on rumours that Nomura Securities soon would issue warrants on Taiwan's Big Three state Banks -- Chang Hwa, First and Hua Nan. Chang Hwa rose T$2 to T$157, First rose T$3 to T$167 and Hua Nan rose T$2.5 to T$128.
"I've checked with our Hong Kong office, but still we cannot confirm whether we have the plan or not," Nomura's Huang said.
The market ignored news that Hualon group head Oung Ta-ming had been imprisoned for four years for stock manipulation and involvement in a share payment default scandal.
"The market has disregarded the news and there are rumours that Hualon has entered the market to boost its own share price," said Michasel Hung, research chief at Nikko Securities.
Hualon Corp was the session's most active issue on Friday, ending up 30 cents or 1.16 percent at T$26.2.
Brokers said they expected a firming trend and a possible testing of resistance at 7,000 points in coming sessions.
